symbols.name: digit width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each digit, a positive integer.
symbols.quote: The digit width $b$ is the number of bits in each digit.

symbols.name: digit count
symbols.meaning: The number of digits in each input.
symbols.quote: Let $N = \lceil n/b\rceil$ be the number of digits in each input.

symbols.name: digit of x
symbols.meaning: The digit of $x$ at position $i$, with weight $(2^b)^i$.
symbols.quote: Let $x_i$ be the digit of $x$ at position $i$, for $0 \le i \le N-1$, so that $x = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} x_i (2^b)^i$.

symbols.name: digit of y
symbols.meaning: The digit of $y$ at position $j$, with weight $(2^b)^j$.
symbols.quote: The digits $y_j$ of $y$ are defined the same way, with position $j$.

symbols.name: formal variable
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomials $P_x$ and $P_y$, which is set to $2^b$ to recover the inputs.
symbols.quote: Let $z$ be a formal variable (the letter $z$ changes meaning here).

symbols.name: polynomial of x
symbols.meaning: The polynomial in $z$ whose coefficients are the digits of $x$.
symbols.quote: Let $P_x(z) = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} x_i z^i$ be the polynomial of $x$, and $P_y(z) = \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} y_j z^j$ that of $y$.

symbols.name: polynomial of y
symbols.meaning: The polynomial in $z$ whose coefficients are the digits of $y$.
symbols.quote: Let $P_x(z) = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} x_i z^i$ be the polynomial of $x$, and $P_y(z) = \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} y_j z^j$ that of $y$.

symbols.name: product coefficient
symbols.meaning: The integer coefficient of $z^k$ in the product $P_x(z)P_y(z)$, which is the $k$-th entry of the convolution of the digit sequences.
symbols.quote: Let $c_k$ be the integer coefficient of $z^k$ in the product $P_x(z)P_y(z)$.

relations.quote: Radix-digit convolution is a reduction of [exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) that writes each input as a polynomial in a power of two whose coefficients are its digits, so that the product becomes a convolution of short integer coefficients.
The convolution is computed with [Fourier transforms](discrete-fourier-transform.md), and each transform level applies [Butterfly](butterfly.md) operations to the whole array.
